title: The Last Grove
dek: Physisia’s last foothold in Voraketh: a living refuge of weathered stone, costly communion and a forest threatened by devouring and spores.

facts.Position: Inland from the perimeter, outside the deeper wasteland
facts.Central features: Ancient tree · altar · standing stones · shallow water
facts.Known refuge: Physisia’s last remaining point of contact
facts.Chronology: Dates mark recorded visits; the local calendar is unconfirmed

sources: Last Grove chronicle · modern visits, communions, discoveries and outbreak
imageAlt: The Last Grove: a weathered tree beside a circular pool and carved stones in dense woodland.
body:
The Last Grove is an ancient druidic sanctuary in Voraketh, inland from the perimeter and outside the deeper wasteland bounded by the Chains. A weathered tree stands within stone rings, shallow water and rough pillars. Abandoned lean-tos offer shelter beneath a forest that is green, strangely ordered and increasingly sick.

For Physisia, it is more than a refuge. She tells Pappy that it is the last place on the island she can still touch. Its shelter, nourishment and divine contact make the Grove a base for the adventurers trying to understand what is consuming Voraketh.

The tree, altar and standing stones

The central tree is not much larger than its neighbours. Its age shows in thick, uneven bark, burls and weathering. Its branches grow irregularly toward the sun, unlike the repeating arrangements of the surrounding forest. Coralyn finds the tree itself natural; the sanctuary around it has been deliberately shaped.

Soil, a stone ring, shallow clean water, roots and natural paving stones form the altar system. Rough standing pillars surround it, with the woodland held back from the circle. Nearby lean-tos predate the present company, although their builders are unknown.

Anky’s investigation finds that the tree and stonework share magic resembling Druid Grove, but older and stronger than its modern formulation. A circle of casters working over a long period is his explanation. The pillars’ invisible writing is separate from that underlying magic; Pappy later recognises it as Druidic.

A green refuge with a broken cycle

Coralyn’s searches find very few animals, with most detected life near the perimeter. Rabbits and small birds survive, while the deeper island grows quieter. Sildithas suggests that the loss of herbivores may have starved predators; that remains his explanation for the imbalance.

Berries near the central tree sustain Pappy almost like Goodberries. Ordinary seasonal rhythms are harder to find. Leaves elsewhere can remain at strange stages of decay, while Alfred observes no fallen leaves around the central tree. Lush vegetation alone does not mean that the island’s ecology is healthy.

Pappy’s communion with Physisia

On 20 October 2025, Pappy attempts to attune to the tree. After roughly an hour, something roots into his consciousness. His body remains beside his companions, but Coralyn cannot reach his ordinary awareness. Through the tree, he meets Physisia.

You kneel in my grove. Much of what that place was has been taken from me. Once my favorite. Now you stand in the last place I touch.Physisia

Pappy pledges to help restore what she has lost. The contact leaves him with two levels of exhaustion. Later, he offers spell slots and vitality to strengthen the connection. Physisia’s voice strains and fades; communion costs both the weakened presence and the person reaching her.

Find Deyara Thorne

Find Deyara Thorne. She was once a leader of the people. Be careful of Talan's creatures for they hold back what was lost.Physisia

Physisia says she has not seen Deyara or those associated with her for a very long time and hopes they are safe. Pappy may tell her that Physisia sent him. The instruction gives the search a historic connection to leadership, but no current location or fate.

Deyara’s name appears in other accounts with different spellings and a troubling difficulty being preserved in Nuru’s memory book. These clues do not identify her as the Maw’s figure, the Destroyer or the voice later heard in the tree.

Anky’s vision of the island

Touching the tree on 7 November 2025 gives Anky a view beyond the sanctuary: repeating forest, enormous Chains, ruined woodland, then the disappearance of soil and stone into nothing. The central absence feels like the Void, but more destructive. Thinking too deeply about it pulls at his mind.

His vision places the Grove toward the surviving outer land, with the Chains between it and the devastated interior. It supplies a relationship between places, rather than a precise survey. The Grove has no confirmed pin on Anky’s later map.

The ancient druidic warning

Pappy recognises the invisible script as a more extensive form of the secret writing his mother used at the hot springs. The translated inscription speaks of druids drinking from the world’s living essence to deepen their connection and protect the wild. At first the forest grows stronger. Then closeness becomes need, and feeding continues because separation feels like loss.

Union without limit is not harmony.Ancient Druidic inscription

The inscription describes an older failure of restraint. It does not say that these druids created the present devouring, or identify what they drew from the heart of the world.

Motes returned to the tree

Ithilrûnë identifies a recovered mote as raw chaos. Sildithas relays her theory that the island’s order and chaos have been forcibly separated, rather than naturally mixed. The tree absorbs motes brought back from beyond the Chains.

Most offerings produce no obvious large change. After an orb enters the tree on 21 January 2026, however, a songbird is heard and a huge gnat on fungus appears. Sildithas later proposes that motes nourish Physisia or the presence sustaining the Grove. The observations suggest a connection with living complexity, without establishing a complete restoration method.

Desecration, exclusion and the devouring

On 10 April 2026, an infernal act associated with Alfred provokes powerful revulsion. Most of the company struggle even to turn toward the Grove. Sildithas forces his way in, apologises and asks Physisia how to help.

She calls the Grove her final refuge and condemns both the disrespect and the weakening of Talan’s defence of the land. Her words complicate the idea that the Chains can simply be broken to free the island.

Stop the devouring.Physisia

Sildithas proposes confronting the threat beyond the Chains before severing them. A warmth and contrary breeze follow, which he takes as approval. Physisia does not verbally confirm his whole plan. Her instruction remains to stop the devouring.

Coralyn’s choice and Alfred’s return

On 29 August 2026, Coralyn brings two motes to the tree. As the first is absorbed, the forest rumbles and trees move. An unfamiliar voice that feels unclean offers her a powerful item or the life of a friend. Asked which friend, it names Alfred.

Coralyn chooses Alfred. A bulbous growth rots away, spores erupt, and she becomes violently ill. Trees fall elsewhere in the forest. Alfred appears alive and healthy, and the second mote is absorbed.

The voice is not identified as Physisia. Coralyn later calls it the “grumpy voice,” and Sildithas says he has never encountered it. Alfred’s return and the outbreak occur together; the voice’s identity and exact bargain mechanism remain unknown.

The fiend and the spreading spores

By 3–4 September, the infection has spread beyond the central tree. Angry black mushrooms with faint red lines appear through the woodland. The spores are necrotic, unnatural and nauseating. The forest’s repetitive growth leaves it with little of the diversity that might resist a spreading disease.

When Pappy communes again, the voice sounds like an elderly woman sick in bed. Physisia tells him that a fiend has invaded the forest and confirms a connection with Alfred’s return.

It is in the forest. It will not cross the chains. Beyond that.... I do not know.Physisia

The fiend’s identity, the reason it will not cross the Chains and the means of curing the spores remain unresolved. The infection outside the Chains and the devouring deeper within the island are simultaneous threats, rather than one proven enemy.

The people who keep returning

Pappy tends the connection with Physisia and gives magic and vitality. Coralyn studies the ecology, brings motes and chooses Alfred’s life. She also successfully returns by teleportation using a leaf from the central tree; why it provides such a strong anchor is unknown.

St. Anky investigates the stones, magic and island geography. Ithilrûnë studies the motes and threats beyond the Chains. Sildithas mediates after the desecration and increasingly treats the sanctuary’s protection as his duty.

Murr is remembered as using the name Last Grove and speaking of lost cycles and animals that remember the island’s earlier life. Those conversations are reported by the adventurers here. Paco guides the early company to shelter; Alfred’s history joins the exclusion ward, his later death and the costly return.

A sanctuary still under threat

What is devouring the island? Where is Deyara? Who spoke through the tree to restore Alfred? Can the spores be cured without harming the Grove? Sildithas later calls the tree a conduit and “likely prison” for Physisia, but imprisonment remains his interpretation.

The ancient warning, Talan’s defences, the motes and Physisia’s pleas offer different pieces of the crisis. The Grove remains a place of refuge and care, with no confirmed simple act that will restore everything it has lost.
